prompt: Engineers use the chat app for quick technical questions, while the sales team uses the same app mostly to share client news.
tells: while the sales team uses the same app mostly to share client news
why: One tool turns into two different tools depending on who uses it. Groups using the same tool in very different ways is the point.
trap: It isn't a shared object they coordinate around; each team just uses it their own way.

prompt: The company bought a full project tool, but most teams ignore its features and use it only as a to-do list.
tells: ignore its features and use it only as a to-do list
why: What the tool becomes depends on how people actually use it, not on its feature list. That's the same tool used differently.
trap: They aren't going around the tool; they're using a small part of it.

prompt: Finance uses the spreadsheet tool for complex models, while the events team uses it as a guest list.
tells: while the events team uses it as a guest list
why: The same software means very different things to two groups. One tool, different uses in practice.
trap: They aren't sharing one spreadsheet, so it isn't a shared object.

prompt: Two hospitals install the identical records system, and a year later their staff work with it in completely different ways.
tells: their staff work with it in completely different ways
why: The same software became different in each place through everyday use. The technology in practice depends on who uses it and how.
trap: Nothing says the tool or routines kept changing each other; they simply diverged in use.

prompt: In one office the shared calendar is for booking rooms; in another, people block time on it to signal they're busy.
tells: people block time on it to signal they're busy
why: The same calendar does different jobs in different offices. Use, not the tool's design, decided what it is.
trap: It does open a possibility, but the tell is the contrast between two groups' uses.

prompt: Teenagers use the family tablet mainly for messaging, while their grandparents use it almost only for video calls.
tells: while their grandparents use it almost only for video calls
why: One device, two quite different tools depending on who holds it. Same tool, different use.
trap: The contrast between groups is the clue, not one new possibility.
